jobs.title: Incident Management Consultant (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
* Securian Financial Group’s internal position title is Infrastructure Consultant.

Position Summary:
The Incident Management Consultant serves as the process owner and subject matter expert for incident and major incident management within IT Service Management, accountable for defining, governing, and continuously improving practices that protect enterprise service availability, minimize business disruption, and enable rapid restoration of services relied upon across the organization.

The role leads and oversees major incident response across the full lifecycle, including maintaining 24/7/365 availability for high-severity incidents, and facilitates end-user and executive-facing communication during both business and after-hours events. The consultant partners closely with technology and business leaders to ensure incidents are managed in alignment with enterprise business impact, risk tolerance, regulatory requirements, and service commitments affecting both customer-facing and internal operations.

In addition to operational leadership, the consultant develops and sustains capabilities for incident trending, problem identification, and availability reporting, translating operational data into insights that support enterprise risk awareness, service reliability, and operational decision-making. The role collaborates closely with Problem & Knowledge Management, REO operations and engineering teams, platform teams, and leadership to strengthen governance, transparency, and outcomes that extend beyond IT into broader business performance.

Responsibilities include but not limited to:
- Own and govern end-to-end incident management: Lead process design, governance standards, operating procedures, and continuous improvement for incident and major incident management; serve as the authoritative point of accountability for how incidents are identified, prioritized, escalated, communicated, and managed through resolution to ensure consistent execution, business continuity, and organizational resilience.
- Support and lead major incident response and communication: Partner with on-call technology leaders coordinating cross-functional service restoration while acting as the incident management SME; lead executive and business-facing communications with consistent, timely, and accurate updates aligned to standards, including 24/7/365 participation and after-hours stakeholder and executive engagement to support informed decision-making during high-impact events.
- Establish standards, enforce adherence, and manage escalations: Define clear expectations for incident execution across internal teams and external service providers; oversee adherence to escalation models, runbooks, and operational standards; and serve as the escalation point for process, communication, and cross-domain coordination issues impacting enterprise operations.
- Develop data-driven insight and improvement capabilities: Design, implement, and continuously enhance incident trending, problem identification, and availability reporting using ServiceNow data to identify recurring incidents, systemic issues, service availability risks, and reliability trends; use these insights to inform problem management engagement, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives that improve service reliability and reduce operational risk across technology and business services.
- Align practices with enterprise priorities and governance: Partner with technology leadership and business stakeholders to ensure incident, major incident, and availability practices align with enterprise business priorities and service commitments; contribute to governance forums, prepare leadership-level reporting, and advise on improvements to processes, metrics, communication models, and service reliability outcomes that support organizational objectives.

Qualifications:
- 3-5+ years expertise in incident management and major incident management, including governance models, escalation frameworks, and executive level communication during critical incidents.
- Strong working knowledge of problem management concepts, including trend analysis, recurrence identification, and collaboration with problem owners to drive root cause outcomes.
- 3-5+ years of advanced, hands on experience with ServiceNow ITSM, specifically Incident and Major Incident processes, SLAs, priority models, notifications, and reporting.
- Proven ability to design and maintain ServiceNow dashboards and analytics, including incident trends, problem indicators, service availability reporting, and operational risk insights.
- Strong understanding of SLA/OLA structures, service availability models, service criticality, priority matrices, categorization and taxonomy design, and tiered escalation models.
- Calm, accountable leadership under pressure: Leads major incidents with clear, authoritative communication, maintaining ownership and presence in 24/7/365 high visibility situations.
- Influential cross-functional coordination: Drives alignment and action across technology teams, problem owners, and business stakeholders without direct authority, using strong facilitation skills.
- Data-driven continuous improvement: Applies strong analytical thinking to translate incident and availability data into executive-ready insights, proactively driving measurable service reliability improvements.

Preferred Qualifications:
- ITIL 4 Foundation/Specialist certification.
- ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) or Certified Implementation Specialist – IT Service Management (CIS‑ITSM).
- Experience using ServiceNow Performance Analytics to support incident trending, problem identification, and availability insights.
- Familiarity with integrating incident and availability data into problem management and service improvement workflows .
- Experience operating as a recognized subject matter expert within a complex, matrixed technology organization.
- Comfort operating in ambiguity and helping establish structure, standards, and governance in evolving or maturing operating models.

#LI-Hybrid **This position will have a hybrid working arrangement, working in-office for a minimum of 3 days a week.**

Securian Financial believes in hybrid work as an integral part of our culture. Associates get the benefit of working both virtually and in our offices. If you’re in a commutable distance (90 minutes) you’ll join us 3 days each week in our offices to collaborate and build relationships. Our policy allows flexibility for the reality of business and personal schedules.

Preferred Skills:
Cross-Functional Collaboration, Cross-Functional Coordination, Incident Management, Problem Solving, ServiceNow Platform
The estimated base pay range for this job is:

$89,000.00 - $164,300.00
Pay may vary depending on job-related factors and individual experience, skills, knowledge, etc. More information on base pay and incentive pay (if applicable) can be discussed with a member of the Securian Financial Talent Acquisition team.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Director - Employee Benefits (Atlantic)
jobs.description:
Overview:

The Regional Sales Director is responsible for driving profitable growth across Securian Financial's employee benefits portfolio, including Group Life, AD&D, and Supplemental Health/Voluntary Benefits , within an assigned geographic territory.

This field-focused role develops and executes a comprehensive territory sales strategy in partnership with the Regional Sales Vice President. The Regional Sales Director builds and maintains strong relationships with channel partners, strategic partners, and employers; identifies and develops new business opportunities; generates and manages RFP activity; and leads opportunities through the sales process to successful close.

The role serves employers and their channel partners with sophisticated benefits and financial needs and requires a highly consultative approach. Success requires the ability to understand client and channel partner needs, connect needs across Securian's product portfolio, and develop differentiated solutions using creativity, flexibility, business acumen, and persuasive communication.

The Regional Sales Director is expected to develop deep knowledge across Securian's employee benefits solutions and bring the appropriate product, underwriting, implementation, and service expertise into opportunities as needed.

Key Responsibilities:
- Own and execute the territory sales strategy across Group Life, AD&D, and Supplemental Health/Voluntary Benefits to achieve profitable growth, sales, and market-development objectives. This role supports a portion of our Atlantic territory, including Ohio, West Virginia, Virginia, Maryland, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine.
- Develop and expand channel partner relationships within the assigned territory, identifying opportunities to deepen existing relationships and establish new relationships that increase Securian's market presence and opportunity pipeline.
- Generate new business opportunities through proactive prospecting, channel partner engagement, strategic partnerships, market development, and employer engagement.
- Manage the sales process from opportunity identification through close, including prospecting, opportunity qualification, RFP assessment and submission, proposal development, channel partner and employer discussions, finalist presentations, negotiations, and follow-up.
- Apply a consultative, multi-product approach to understand employer needs and identify opportunities to position Life and Supplemental Health solutions individually or as an integrated benefits solution.
- Partner closely with the Regional Sales Vice President to develop territory priorities, coordinate sales activity, pursue strategic opportunities, and deliver against overall territory objectives.
- Collaborate with sales enablement, product, underwriting, client relationships, strategic partnerships and enrollment, implementation, and other internal partners to develop competitive solutions and successfully navigate complex opportunities.
- Develop and deliver compelling sales presentations that clearly articulate Securian's value proposition and differentiate its products, capabilities, and service model.
- Develop annual channel partner engagement strategies and measurable objectives in partnership with Sales Enablement and Client Relationship teams; monitor progress and adjust strategies based on results and market opportunities.
- Maintain accurate and timely opportunity, pipeline, activity, and relationship information in Salesforce and use data to prioritize activity, identify trends, and improve territory performance.
- Provide competitive and market intelligence gathered through channel partner, employer, and field interactions to inform product strategy, capabilities, process improvements, and broader business strategy.
- Serve as a voice of the market by identifying emerging customer needs, competitive trends, and opportunities to strengthen Securian's employee benefits value proposition.

Qualifications:
- Proven successful sales experience, within employee benefits, insurance, financial services, or a similarly complex business-to-business sales environment.
- Demonstrated ability to generate and secure sales within the mid-to-large employer market and successfully manage complex, consultative sales cycles.
- Broad knowledge of the group benefits and insurance ecosystem, with expertise in Life, AD&D, and Voluntary Benefits. Knowledge of Disability and Absence Solutions is preferred, particularly as it supports a consultative approach for positioning Life solutions within an employer’s broader benefits strategy.
- Proven professionalism and integrity, with a consistent track record of exercising sound judgment, honoring commitments, and building credibility and trust in all internal and external interactions.
- Demonstrated ability to develop, maintain, and expand productive channel partner and client relationships.
- Strong business and financial acumen and ability to understand employer benefit needs and position solutions across multiple products and capabilities.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including demonstrated ability to deliver effective presentations and communicate with channel partners, employers, senior decision-makers, and internal stakeholders.
- Strong persuasion, negotiation, and influencing skills with the ability to overcome objections and navigate complex sales situations.
- Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to assess opportunities, analyze information and data, identify trends, and determine appropriate courses of action.
- Demonstrated initiative, creativity, and persistence in developing sales strategies, prospecting for new opportunities, and advancing opportunities through the sales cycle.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and time-sensitive opportunities with a strong sense of urgency, attention to detail, and accountability for results.
- Ability to collaborate effectively across Sales, Client Relationship, Product, Underwriting, Implementation, and other internal teams.
- Comfortably operating in an evolving environment and adapting to changing market conditions, priorities, products, and strategies.
- Proactive and self-directed, with the ability to act with limited supervision and a strong orientation toward achieving established goals and performance metrics.
- Ability to travel approximately 50% of the time.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
- Active Life and health insurance license.

jobs.title: Director of Regulatory Compliance (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
*At Securian Financial the internal position title is Compliance Dir.* ​

Position Overview
Securian Financial is seeking an experienced and forward-thinking  Director of Regulatory Compliance  to lead and continue the evolution of our enterprise regulatory compliance program. Reporting directly to the Chief Compliance Officer, this leader will have an opportunity to shape how regulatory compliance partners with our business lines, identifies emerging risks, and enables responsible growth across the organization.

This is a highly visible leadership role for someone who brings deep insurance and regulatory expertise along with the ability to lead transformation. You’ll build upon a strong foundation and  established teams while advancing a more proactive, integrated and data-driven approach to compliance risk management.

What you will do:
- Lead Securian’s enterprise regulatory compliance program and a team of approximately 20 associates, including leaders responsible for compliance sub-teams.

- Provide oversight across a broad range of regulatory compliance activities, including life insurance and annuity product administration, securities-related activities, complaint handling and tracking, suitability and replacements, unclaimed property, and related monitoring and oversight.

- Partner across Securian’s business lines and Operations teams to understand business priorities, identify regulatory risks and develop practical approaches to managing those risks.

- Evaluate and evolve the Regulatory Compliance operating model, creating clarity around team responsibilities, accountabilities and ways of working.

- Strengthen proactive compliance risk identification, assessment, monitoring, quantification, reporting and escalation.

- Oversee the develop and enhancement of policies, training, tools and monitoring practices that support effective regulatory compliance and risk mitigation.

- Translate complex regulatory requirements and compliance risks into practical business guidance that enables informed decision-making.

- Anticipate regulatory developments and emerging risks and help the organization respond proactively.

- Develop future compliance leaders and build organizational capabilities that position the function for long-term success.

What success looks like:
In this role, you will help move Regulatory Compliance toward an increasingly proactive and integrated model—one where responsibilities are clear, compliance teams work effectively together, and business partners view Compliance as both a trusted advisor and an effective independent risk management function. Over time, you will advance the use of consistent and increasingly automated monitoring of key compliance risks and strengthen the policies and programs needed to respond to regulatory change, emerging risks and opportunities for improvement.

What we are looking for:
We’re looking for an accomplished compliance leader who understands the complexity of operating within a highly regulated insurance environment and has successfully led meaningful change within a compliance organization.

Required qualifications:
- 15+ years of relevant experience in compliance, risk, legal or regulatory functions.

- Significant experience within the insurance industry.

- 5+ years of leadership experience.

- Demonstrated experience leading leaders and developing high-performing teams.

- Experience influencing senior leaders and partnering across multiple business areas.

- Experience navigating complex regulatory requirements and providing practical, business-oriented compliance guidance.

- Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to establish credibility with both business partners and compliance professionals.

Preferred qualifications:
- Experience leading significant compliance program enhancements or transformation within an insurance organization.

- Experience leading teams through organizational redesign or changes to a compliance operating model.

- Experience managing regulatory examinations and interactions with regulators.

- Broad familiarity with individual insurance, employer voluntary benefits, specialty lines insurance and securities-related activities.

- Juris Doctor (JD) degree.

A successful leader in this role will bring credibility, curiosity and a practical mindset to the work. You will be comfortable challenging existing approaches when needed, creating clarity in complex environments and bringing people along through change. Most importantly, you will help build a Regulatory Compliance organization that enables Securian Financial to move with confidence—supporting the business in growing responsibly while effectively identifying and managing regulatory risk.

#LI-hybrid **This position will be in a hybrid working arrangement.**

Securian Financial believes in hybrid work as an integral part of our culture. Associates get the benefit of working both virtually and in our offices. If you’re in a commutable distance (90 minutes), you’ll join us 3 days each week in our offices to collaborate and build relationships. Our policy allows flexibility for the reality of business and personal schedules.

Preferred Skills:
Compliance Analysis, Compliance Oversight, Compliance Programs, Data Management, External Communication, Internal Communications, Policy Development, Process Improvements, Regulatory Compliance, Regulatory Interpretation, Risk Analysis, Risk Assessments

jobs.title: Actuarial Consultant - Enterprise Risk Management (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
*At Securian Financial the internal title for this position is Actuarial Consultant.*

Position Overview

This role supports Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) by contributing to enterprise financial risk initiatives across insurance risk, asset liability management (ALM), and broader risk management. Working with teams across the organization, this role provides analysis, coordination, and governance support that helps inform risk-aware business decisions.

Responsibilities include but not limited to:
Enterprise Financial Risk Management
- Advance enterprise financial risk initiatives by developing analyses, leading workstreams, and contributing to risk-informed strategic decisions.

- Partner across Solutions Groups, Finance, Actuarial, and Asset Management to solve complex business challenges and deliver enterprise-wide initiatives.

- Strengthen enterprise risk governance by enhancing risk frameworks, policies, reporting, and governance processes that support effective decision making.

- Translate technical analyses into clear, actionable insights for a variety of stakeholders, including senior leadership.

Asset Liability Management
- Provide subject matter expertise on Asset Liability Management by developing and enhancing enterprise frameworks for interest rate, liquidity, equity, and credit risk, while helping ensure these risks are appropriately understood and managed.

- Coordinate ALM governance, including the Asset Liability Management (ALM) Working Group, to facilitate cross-functional discussions, connect enterprise initiatives, and support effective decision making.

- Partner with Solutions Groups and Securian Asset Management to develop asset liability management strategies that balance risk, return, capital efficiency, and business objectives, while supporting the Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA) process.

Insurance Risk
- Lead analytical workstreams supporting insurance risk initiatives, including risk capacity, reinsurance, emerging risks, and the continued development of the enterprise insurance risk framework.

- Strengthen enterprise insurance risk governance by supporting the Mortality Oversight Group (MOG), developing analyses, and facilitating cross-functional discussions that enhance the enterprise's understanding and management of insurance risk.

Qualifications:
- ASA, FSA, or significant progress toward actuarial designation.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.

- Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to navigate complex and ambiguous problems.

- Ability to adapt in a dynamic environment, manage competing priorities, and learn new concepts quickly.

- Demonstrated initiative, ownership, and accountability in managing work and delivering results.

- Proven ability to build collaborative relationships and work effectively across functions.

- Experience managing analytical projects and developing recommendations to support business decisions.

jobs.title: Director, Third Party Risk Management & Transformation (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
***At Securian, the internal job title is Risk Management Consulting Director.

Position Summary
This is a hands-on, working Director role for an experienced Third Party Risk Management leader who wants to shape and transform an enterprise program. Leading a small team, this individual will serve as Securian's TPRM subject matter expert while personally driving the strategy, design, transformation, and continued maturation of the program. The Director will work across Procurement, Law & Compliance, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Technology, and business leadership to establish scalable practices across the third-party lifecycle. Success in this role requires more than oversight—the Director will actively develop solutions, influence stakeholders, solve complex third-party risk issues, and champion TPRM practices across the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities (include but are not limited to)

Strategic Leadership & Enterprise Partnership (25%)
- Define and execute an enterprise TPRM strategy aligned to risk appetite, business priorities, and the evolving external environment
- Influence senior leaders to drive consistent adoption of TPRM practices and proactive third-party risk management across Solution Groups
- Lead cross-functional alignment across the third-party ecosystem, fostering strong partnerships with Procurement, Compliance, BCM, Cybersecurity, and other second-line risk functions
- Communicate TPRM program status and risk insights to executive stakeholders, including Risk Council and Executive Leadership Team

Program Transformation & Delivery (30%)
- Transform the TPRM program operating model, governance, processes, and enabling technology
- Drive scalability and efficiency improvements across the full third-party lifecycle
- Establish and execute a capability maturity roadmap aligned to industry best practices while managing to a defined program budget

Third Party Risk Oversight & Governance (25%)
- Provide enterprise oversight of third-party risks across operational, cybersecurity, privacy, financial, and regulatory domains
- Ensure consistent risk tiering, due diligence, ongoing monitoring, and issue remediation practices
- Maintain audit and regulatory readiness through strong documentation and defensible risk decisions

Talent Development & Team Leadership (20%)
- Lead and develop a high-performing TPRM team and aligned operational risk resources
- Establish clear roles, expectations, accountability, and development pathways
- Foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and shared ownership of risk

Required Qualifications

- Demonstrated experience building, designing, and transforming enterprise-wide third party risk management or operational risk programs and operating models within a complex environment
- Strong knowledge of third-party risk domains including operational, cybersecurity, privacy, financial, and regulatory risk
- Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional alignment
- Experience managing regulatory expectations, audits, and risk governance structures

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience in financial services, insurance, or other highly regulated industries
- Hands-on experience with TPRM enabling technologies and automation tools
- 12+ years of experience leading Third Party Risk Management or operational risk programs in a complex enterprise environment
- Advanced degree or professional risk management certification (e.g., CRMP, CISA, CISSP)
